paper.title: Distributed Learning in Multi-Armed Bandit with Multiple Players

settings.name_in_paper: Decentralized MAB with M distributed players
unmapped: M (canonical N) players each choose one of K arms with no communication; system regret against the sum of the M best means
Collision model 1: colliding players share the reward (only one obtains it); collision model 2: no colliding player gets reward
Single-parameter reward family f(s;theta) satisfying Lai-Robbins regularity conditions C1-C4 (and C5 for point estimates / confidence bounds)
settings.definition_quote: There are $M$ distributed players competing for $N$ independent arms. Each arm, when played, offers i.i.d. reward according to a distribution with an unknown parameter. At each time, each player chooses one arm to play without exchanging observations or any information with other players. Players choosing the same arm collide, and, depending on the collision model, either no one receives reward or the colliding players share the reward in an arbitrary way.

algorithms.name: TDFS policy pi*_F (with pre-agreement on offsets), built on Lai-Robbins policy
TDFS policy pi*_F without pre-agreement (random offsets)

symbols.L_Theta: centralized Lai-Robbins/Anantharam constant sum_{j: mu_j < mu_sigma(M)} (mu_sigma(M) - mu_j)/I(theta_j, theta_sigma(M)), per the proof

conditions: the M best arms have distinct nonnegative means

source.label: thm:optorder
source.quote: Under both collision models, the optimal order of the system regret growth rate of the decentralized MAB is logarithmic, \ie for an optimal decentralized policy $\pi^*$, we have L(\Theta)\le\liminf_{T\rightarrow\infty}\frac{R_T^{\pi^*}(\Theta)}{\log T}\le\limsup_{T\rightarrow\infty}\frac{R_T^{\pi^*}(\Theta)}{\log T}\le U(\Theta) for some constants $L(\Theta)$ and $U(\Theta)$ that depend on $\Theta$.

results.notes: Theorem states only existence of constants; the proof identifies L(Theta) with the centralized bound via Lemma 1. Paper's M players = canonical N, paper's N arms = K. Upper part is realized by Theorem 2.

symbols.sum_top: sum over i = 1..M of the M best arms
symbols.sum_below: sum over arms n with mu_n < mu_sigma(M)
symbols.mu_sigma_i: mean of the i-th best arm

conditions: the M best arms have distinct nonnegative means
tuning: Lai-Robbins point estimates and confidence bounds satisfying C5

source.label: thm:worstcase
source.quote: Under the TDFS policy $\pi^*_F$, we have, for some constant $C(\Theta)$, \limsup_{T\rightarrow\infty}\frac{R^{\pi^*_F}_T(\Theta)}{\log T}\le C(\Theta). ... Under collision model 1, C(\Theta)=M(\Sigma_{i=1}^Mx_k\mu(\theta_{\sigma(i)})-\Sigma_{n:\mu(\theta_n)<\mu(\theta_{\sigma(M)})}\frac{\mu(\theta_{n})}{I(\theta_{n},\theta_{\sigma(M)})}).

results.notes: Paper writes x_k inside sum over i (typo; appendix uses x_i). Canonical N = number of players (paper's M). Theorem 3 (fairness) states each player's local regret rate is 1/M of the system rate.

symbols.sum_top: sum over i = 1..M of the M best arms
symbols.sum_below: sum over arms n with mu_n < mu_sigma(M)
symbols.sum_k_x: (1/M) * sum_{k=1}^M x_k, so that N*sum_k_x = sum_k x_k
symbols.mu_sigma_i: mean of the i-th best arm

conditions: the M best arms have distinct nonnegative means
tuning: Lai-Robbins point estimates and confidence bounds satisfying C5
results.notes: Expression encoded with declared symbols; awkward sum_k_x scaling used to keep sum_k x_k = N*sum_k_x. Simpler: C = M(sum_k x_k * sum_i mu_sigma(i) - ...).

conditions: the M best arms have distinct nonnegative means

source.label: thm:optElimPre
source.quote: The decentralized TDFS policy $\pi_F^*$ without pre-agreement is order-optimal and fair.

results.notes: Order-optimal means logarithmic regret growth with an unspecified Theta-dependent constant.

symbols.sum_below: sum over arms j with mu_j < mu_sigma(M)

conditions: policy is uniformly good and belongs to the Time Division Selection (TDS) class

source.label: thm:lowerboundTDS
source.quote: For any uniformly good decentralized policy $\pi$ in the TDS class, we have \liminf_{T\rightarrow\infty}\frac{R_T^{\pi}(\Theta)}{\log T}\ge\Sigma_{i=1}^M\Sigma_{j:\mu(\theta_j)<\mu(\theta_{\sigma(M)})}\frac{\mu(\theta_{\sigma(M)})-\mu(\theta_{j})}{I(\theta_{j},\theta_{\sigma(i)})}.

results.notes: Algorithm class: uniformly good TDS policies (fixed Theta-independent time portions a_ij of playing the j-th best arm).
